_meta.training_eligible_reason: Diagnostic/adjudication artifact for the H4 mechanism (B2M-KO ligandome collapse) on clean single-allele lines and for localizing the A375 B2M-KO anomaly. Not a training corpus; a recipe + feasibility record. Any promotion still requires the H4 kill-test / leave-HLA-out advantage, which this deposit cannot supply (A*02-only, not disjoint-allele).
_meta.goal: Reprocess PXD063813 raw timsTOF DIA with a NO-ENZYME (unspecific) search to recover the true HLA-I ligandome, then test whether B2M-KO collapses the ligandome in C1R-A*02 and K562-A*02 (HLA-null single-allele transfectants). Collapse => confirms H4 on clean defined-allele lines and localizes the earlier A375 88%-retention anomaly to A375 (leaky KO / MHC1-TIP) rather than A*02 biology.
_meta.why_reprocess: The deposit's HELD processed file (report.pr_matrix.tsv etc.) is a TRYPTIC WHOLE-PROTEOME DIA-NN search (--cut K*,R*, missed-cleavages 1, avg peptide length 14.3, ~7800 proteins/run). Proteome is unchanged by B2M-KO (as expected), so the held matrix's KO/WT ~0.96-0.99 detection ratio does NOT reflect antigen presentation. The eluted HLA-I ligandome requires a fresh no-enzyme reprocessing of the raw .d files.

blockers: DISK: 5.9 GB free. Raw = 24 .d.zip totalling 145.69 GB; per-file compressed 5.06-6.60 GB (mean 6.07 GB). A single compressed .d.zip (min 5.06 GB) barely fits and leaves NO room to unzip. DIA-NN searches the UNCOMPRESSED .d (a Bruker .d unzips to ~10-15 GB). Even one WT/KO pair (2 files) is physically impossible on 5.9 GB.

SEARCH ENGINE: No no-enzyme-capable DIA/DDA engine installed locally. Probed and NOT found: DIA-NN, MSFragger/FragPipe, philosopher, Comet, MS-GF+. Only Java is present (no mono for Comet, no Docker/Singularity runtime). The only DIA-NN presence on disk is BioMate Galaxy tool XMLs + skill docs (a CLOUD execution path, not a local binary).

ANCHOR REFERENCE: the A*02:01 mono-allelic ligand anchor lives on S3 (s3://knowledge-datasets-1759951976/immunology_sc_corpus_broad/acquisitions/immunopeptidome/monoallelic_ref/combined_monoallelic_hlaI_human.tsv.gz), NOT locally; the task scoped S3 out. The anchor is regenerable from OPEN sources (MHCflurry 2.0 mass_spec CSV + SysteMHC AlleleLibs) but the search itself is still disk/engine-blocked.

DEPOSIT_FACTS.title: The covalent bonding of beta-2-microglobulin with HLA class I influences the antigenic landscape of cells
DEPOSIT_FACTS.instrument: timsTOF Pro 2 (Bruker), nanoLC Dionex UltiMate 3000, DIA high-sensitivity PASEF, 50 min gradient
DEPOSIT_FACTS.acquisition: DIA (diaPASEF), QuantUMS high-precision quant, iodoacetamide (carbamidomethyl C)
DEPOSIT_FACTS.held_search_software: DIA-NN 2.0.0, spectral library from UniProt human reference proteome + B2M-HLA construct translation

cell_lines_and_arms.layout: 2 injections x 3 biological replicates per arm; both lines are HLA-null parents carrying a single defined HLA-A*02 transfectant

reusable_supporting_files_small.fasta: UP000005640_9606_AddedSequence_20250302.fasta (13.7 MB) — UniProt human + the added B2M-HLA construct sequence; REUSE this for the no-enzyme search
reusable_supporting_files_small.report.log.txt: 0.1 MB — original DIA-NN command line (confirms --cut K*,R* --missed-cleavages 1 tryptic search)
reusable_supporting_files_small.report.pr_matrix.tsv: 44.4 MB — TRYPTIC proteome precursor matrix (the misleading held file; NOT a ligandome)

REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.engine: DIA-NN 2.0.0 (match the deposit's own version for comparability; >=1.8.1 also fine). Library-free (predicted spectral library) direct-from-.d diaPASEF search.
REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.fasta: UP000005640_9606_AddedSequence_20250302.fasta (pulled from the deposit; keeps the B2M-HLA construct so construct-derived peptides are searchable).

digest.protease: UNSPECIFIC (no-enzyme). DIA-NN flag: set Cut = '' (empty) i.e. remove --cut, OR GUI Protease = 'unspecific'. Missed cleavages irrelevant for unspecific and should be 0.
digest.diann_cli: --cut  (empty value; explicitly override the deposit's --cut K*,R*)  --missed-cleavages 0

peptide_length_window.rationale: HLA class-I ligandome window. DIA-NN: --min-pep-len 8 --max-pep-len 12 (GUI: Peptide length range 8-12). This is the single most important change vs the tryptic proteome search (which averaged 14.3 and ended 99% in K/R).
peptide_length_window.note: Some HLA-I pipelines use 8-14 to catch longer ligands; keep 8-12 as primary and optionally re-run 8-14 as a sensitivity check.

REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.precursor_charge: --min-pc 1 --max-pc? use 1-4 (HLA-I ligands are predominantly 1-3+). GUI precursor charge 1-4.
REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.mz_ranges: Keep deposit defaults for diaPASEF (precursor + fragment m/z as acquired); DIA-NN auto-detects from .d.

modifications.variable: Oxidation (M) recommended for immunopeptidomics; optionally N-term acetylation. Keep var-mods low (immunopeptidome libraries balloon with unspecific digest).

fdr.note: 1% precursor FDR (--qvalue 0.01). For immunopeptidomics also report a run-specific decoy-based peptide FDR; DIA-NN's global q at 1% is the primary gate. Consider --matrix-qvalue 0.01 for the output matrix.

REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.library_mode: Library-free: --predictor (deep-learning-predicted spectra + RT + IM) generated from the FASTA under the unspecific 8-12 digest. Expect a very large in silico library (unspecific 8-12mers over the human proteome) => high RAM/time; see resource estimate.
REPROCESSING_RECIPE_no_enzyme.quant: QuantUMS / MBR across the 24 runs (--reanalyse for MBR) so WT and KO precursors share the same evidence pool. Keep WT+KO of the same line in one DIA-NN run for a fair within-line comparison.

A02_ANCHOR_SCORING.purpose: Distinguish genuine HLA-A*02:01 ligands from search noise/co-purified background so the KO/WT retention is measured on TRUE presented peptides, not chemical background.

reference.primary: A*02:01 mono-allelic eluted-ligand set from the mono-allelic anchor (combined_monoallelic_hlaI_human.tsv.gz on S3), filter allele == HLA-A*02:01. Regenerable OPEN if S3 unavailable: MHCflurry 2.0 curated_training_data.mass_spec.csv.bz2 (allele HLA-A*02:01, ~thousands of ligands) UNION SysteMHC AlleleLibs A*02:01 pepidx.
reference.predictor_open: MHCflurry 2.0 (pip install mhcflurry; Apache-2.0) OR MixMHCpred (Gfeller lab, OPEN) as a de-novo A*02:01 binding predictor when a peptide is not in the reference set.

A02_ANCHOR_SCORING.genuine_HLA_ligand_definition: A detected 8-12mer is a genuine A*02:01 ligand if EITHER (a) exact-match present in the A*02:01 mono-allelic reference, OR (b) MHCflurry/MixMHCpred %rank <= 2 (strong+weak binder) against HLA-A*02:01. A*02:01 canonical anchors: P2 = L/M/I (Leu dominant), P-Omega(C-term) = V/L/I. As a cheap sanity motif check, expect strong P2-Leu and C-term-Val/Leu enrichment in the WT ligandome.

retention_metric.definition: retention = (# genuine A*02:01 ligands detected in KO, union over KO replicates at 1% FDR) / (# genuine A*02:01 ligands detected in WT).
also_report: Jaccard overlap of genuine-ligand sets KO vs WT
fraction of WT genuine ligands lost in KO
P2/Comega motif entropy WT vs KO (motif should DISAPPEAR on true collapse)

collapse_threshold_interpretation.collapse_CONFIRMS_H4: retention roughly <= 0.15-0.30 AND loss of the A*02:01 P2-Leu/Comega-Val motif in KO. B2M-KO removes surface HLA-I => ligandome collapses. On clean single-allele HLA-null parents (C1R, K562) this is the expected clean-mechanism result.
collapse_threshold_interpretation.partial_or_no_collapse: retention >= ~0.5 with motif retained would mirror the A375 88% anomaly and would argue the KO is leaky or a B2M-independent presentation route persists.
collapse_threshold_interpretation.diagnostic_payoff: If C1R and K562 CLEANLY collapse while A375 retained 88%, the anomaly LOCALIZES to A375 (leaky B2M-KO clone / MHC1-TIP-type sensitivity / residual surface HLA), NOT to A*02 biology or to the H4 mechanism. That is the adjudication value of this run.

RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.storage: ~350-450 GB working disk: 145.7 GB compressed download + ~200-300 GB uncompressed .d (24 x ~10-13 GB) + DIA-NN predicted library + scratch/output. Provision >=500 GB to be safe. (Can process line-by-line to cap peak: one line's 12 runs at a time ~ 150-180 GB.)
RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.download: 145.7 GB over PRIDE FTP/https/Aspera; ~1-4 h depending on link. Aspera (fasp) fastest.
RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.compute: Unspecific 8-12 digest over the human proteome yields a very large predicted library. DIA-NN library generation + search of 24 diaPASEF runs: 32-64 CPU cores, 128-256 GB RAM strongly recommended (unspecific immunopeptidome DIA is RAM-heavy). GPU optional (DIA-NN predictor benefits from it).
RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.wall_time: Rough: predicted-library build 1-3 h; per-run diaPASEF search 15-45 min x 24 = 6-18 h; MBR/reanalyse pass 1-3 h. End-to-end ~10-24 h on a 32-64 core node.
RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.cost_class: 1 large node (e.g. 64 vCPU / 256 GB) for ~1 day, or split by cell line into 2 shorter jobs.
RESOURCE_ESTIMATE_proper_node.execution_route_recommended: BioMate DIA-NN Galaxy tool on AWS Batch (diann tool XMLs already present in repo) — the intended cloud execution path. Feed the deposit FASTA + the 24 .d, override protease->unspecific and length->8-12 per the recipe above. This keeps it on the BioMate execution engine per project policy rather than a local workaround.

NEXT_STEPS_if_run_on_node: 1. Pull the 24 .d.zip (or, minimally, the two lines separately) + UP000005640_9606_AddedSequence_20250302.fasta from PRIDE.
2. DIA-NN 2.0.0 unspecific, len 8-12, 1% FDR, per-line MBR (WT+KO together).
3. Regenerate/pull the A*02:01 anchor; classify detected 8-12mers as genuine ligands (reference match OR MHCflurry %rank<=2).
4. Compute KO/WT genuine-ligand retention + P2/Comega motif for C1R and K562.
5. Compare to A375 88% retention to localize the anomaly.
honesty_notes: No result was fabricated. The B2M-KO ligandome retention for C1R/K562 was NOT computed because the search could not be run (disk + no engine).
The 0.96-0.99 KO/WT numbers in HARD_ESSENTIAL_KO_RESCAN.json are the TRYPTIC PROTEOME matrix and are explicitly NOT a presentation readout; they must not be cited as ligandome retention.
